about: Coordinates are WGS84 decimal degrees. 'areas' are Natural Earth 1:110m rings in GeoJSON [lon, lat] order (tool/build_country_shapes.py). Leaders change: verify before teaching. government_system is one of presidential_republic, parliamentary_republic, constitutional_monarchy, absolute_monarchy. Flags: assets/flags/<iso2>.svg.

pins.name: Aconcagua
pins.description: Highest mountain in the Americas and outside Asia.

pins.name: Ojos del Salado
pins.description: The highest volcano on Earth, on the border with Chile.

pins.name: Lanín
pins.description: A snow-capped stratovolcano in Patagonia.

notes.text: The name Argentina comes from the Latin word 'argentum', meaning silver.
Ushuaia, in Tierra del Fuego, is often called the southernmost city in the world.
Gauchos are the cowboys of the Pampas, famous for horse riding and sharing mate tea.

pins.name: Mount Fuji
pins.description: Japan's tallest peak; it last erupted in 1707.

pins.name: Sakurajima
pins.description: One of the most active volcanoes in Japan.

pins.name: Mount Kita
pins.description: Second-highest mountain in Japan, in the Southern Alps.

notes.text: Japan is made of more than 14,000 islands.
Japanese people call their country 'Nihon' or 'Nippon', meaning 'origin of the sun'.
Children fly carp-shaped streamers called koinobori on Children's Day, 5 May.

pins.name: Mount Catherine
pins.description: Egypt's highest mountain, in the Sinai Peninsula.

pins.name: Mount Sinai
pins.description: Famous peak climbed at night to watch the sunrise.

pins.name: Qattara Depression
pins.description: A huge desert basin far below sea level.

notes.text: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest human-made structure for about 3,800 years.
Almost everyone in Egypt lives close to the Nile, which flows north into the Mediterranean.
Ancient Egyptians wrote with hieroglyphs, a script of more than 700 picture signs.

pins.name: Teide
pins.description: Spain's highest peak, a volcano on the island of Tenerife.

pins.name: Mulhacén
pins.description: Highest mountain on the Iberian Peninsula, in the Sierra Nevada.

pins.name: Aneto
pins.description: The tallest summit of the Pyrenees.

notes.text: Spanish is the second most spoken native language in the world.
Madrid sits almost exactly in the centre of the Iberian Peninsula.
In Buñol, people throw tomatoes at each other every August during La Tomatina.

pins.name: Hvannadalshnúkur
pins.description: Iceland's highest point, on the rim of the Öræfajökull volcano.

pins.name: Hekla
pins.description: Once called the 'Gateway to Hell' in medieval legends.

pins.name: Eyjafjallajökull
pins.description: Its 2010 ash cloud grounded flights across Europe.

notes.text: Iceland sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where two tectonic plates pull apart.
Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest in the world.
Many Icelanders grow up with tales of huldufólk, the 'hidden people' who live in rocks.

pins.name: Pico da Neblina
pins.description: Brazil's highest peak, often hidden in clouds on the Venezuelan border.

notes.text: About 60% of the Amazon rainforest is inside Brazil.
Brasília was built from scratch in under four years and opened in 1960.

pins.name: Villarrica
pins.description: One of Chile's most active volcanoes, overlooking a lake and town.

notes.text: Chile stretches over 4,300 km from north to south, yet averages only 177 km wide.
The Atacama Desert in northern Chile is the driest non-polar desert on Earth.

pins.name: Pico de Orizaba
pins.description: Highest mountain in Mexico and the highest volcano in North America.

pins.name: Popocatépetl
pins.description: Its Nahuatl name means 'Smoking Mountain'.

notes.text: Mexico City was built over the Aztec island capital of Tenochtitlan.
Chocolate, corn and chillies were first cultivated in ancient Mexico.

pins.name: Denali
pins.description: Highest mountain peak in North America, located in Alaska.

pins.name: Badwater Basin
pins.description: Lowest and hottest spot in North America, in Death Valley.

notes.text: The 50 stars on the flag stand for the 50 states, and the 13 stripes for the original colonies.

pins.name: Mount Logan
pins.description: Highest mountain in Canada, in the Yukon.

notes.text: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
More than half of all the natural lakes on Earth are in Canada.

pins.name: Mont Blanc
pins.description: Highest mountain in the Alps and Western Europe.

notes.text: Mainland France is nicknamed 'L'Hexagone' because of its six-sided shape.

pins.name: Mount Etna
pins.description: Europe's tallest active volcano, on the island of Sicily.

pins.name: Mount Vesuvius
pins.description: Famous for burying the Roman city of Pompeii in 79 AD.

notes.text: Two independent micro-states, Vatican City and San Marino, sit entirely inside Italy.

pins.name: Mafadi
pins.description: Highest peak in South Africa, in the Drakensberg range.

notes.text: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria, Cape Town and Bloemfontein.

pins.name: Kangchenjunga
pins.description: Third-highest mountain in the world, on the border with Nepal.

notes.text: Chess (chaturanga) and the number zero were both invented in ancient India.

pins.name: Mount Kosciuszko
pins.description: Mainland Australia's highest peak, in the Snowy Mountains.

pins.name: Kati Thanda–Lake Eyre
pins.description: Lowest natural point in Australia; a salt lake that rarely fills with water.

notes.text: Australia is the only country that covers an entire continent.
